name: use.computer

modes.label: Reserved M4 Mac mini, priced per macOS VM slot (2 VMs per Mac)

sizes.name: split: macOS VM slot = half of a reserved M4 Mac mini (5 CPU / 8 GiB)
whole: one VM per reserved Mac (10 CPU / 16 GiB)

modes.commit_note: Reservation = N Mac minis x X hours (X >= 24), paid up front. Sandboxes inside a reservation are free to create/destroy; the Macs return to the pool when end_at passes.
modes.note: Homepage: "$0.90/hr per Mac", "reserve for 24 hours or more, up to 2 VMs at a time per Mac". Docs: each Mac mini is a stock M4 16 GB / 512 GB SSD and the 2 VMs get "4 cores + 8 GB each". Encoded per VM slot at $0.45/h (= $0.90/2), which assumes VMs are paired; an odd VM count pays for an idle slot. Per-VM disk share not published. min 24 h per reservation (Apple SLA). Hourly granularity after the 24 h minimum is confirmed (OpenAPI: integer hours, minimum 24); an active reservation can be shortened (end >= 24 h after start and >= 5 min from now) with the remaining-time delta returned as account credit, or grown pro rata. 2026-09-28 (patch v3-computer-use): OpenAPI VMLayout: split (default) = two 5 CPU / 8 GiB VMs, whole = one 10 CPU / 16 GiB VM (legacy whole may keep 12 GiB), same per-Mac price. 24 h minimum applies per Mac reservation, not per VM creation.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go reservations
plans.note: No plan fee. Production fleet "currently has 28 Mac minis live" (docs), i.e. at most ~56 concurrent VMs unless more are added.

features.ip_note: No browser-automation API, stealth, CAPTCHA or proxy options documented; browsers (e.g. Safari) are driven via the macOS desktop/shell API.

caveats: Rate resolved 2026-09-29: the live API config that drives the dashboard price calculator returns hourly_rate_cents 90 ($0.90/h per Mac, matching the homepage); the dashboard computes total = Macs x hours x rate. The docs' $1.91/h (Quick start, Lifecycle, llms-full.txt) is stale text.

Billing boundary is the Mac reservation, not the sandbox: you pay 24 h minimum per Mac even for a 10-minute session. Encoded as min_billed_seconds 86400 per VM slot; reserving continuously for the month (730 h) is cheaper than re-reserving daily only when sessions span >~20 h/day.
VM slot price assumes both VM slots of each Mac are used; 1 VM per Mac costs $0.90/h.
VM shape by layout (OpenAPI VMLayout): split 5 CPU / 8 GiB x2 per Mac (default) or whole 10 CPU / 16 GiB x1; larger workloads cannot run. Docs prose says 4 cores + 8 GB per VM (older text).
cold_start_ms 1000 = vendor claim "<1s warm boot" on pre-booted reserved Macs, not measured.
Snapshot storage, egress and regions not published (null). Support contact is support@daytona.io; Daytona routes macOS sandboxes here.

Licensing: Apple permits Mac leasing for "Permitted Developer Services"; general computer-use agent workloads are a grey zone. Apple macOS SLA: leasing a Mac requires a minimum lease of 24 consecutive hours with sole use by the lessee, and allows at most 2 additional macOS VMs per Mac.

Idle VMs (~2 min without HTTP/SSH/VNC) are reaped and replaced by a fresh clone; the Mac reservation keeps billing. Snapshots are portable disk images, no memory resume. Docs rate $1.91/h per Mac re-confirmed on docs.use.computer/docs/concepts 2026-09-28; homepage $0.90 could not be re-rendered this pass, so the conflict stands (at $1.91 the bill is 2.12x).

Payment is prepaid only: reservations are paid from a credit balance or Stripe checkout; credit packs $1-$1,000. No postpaid/overage; if credits are insufficient the reservation (or edit) is refused (HTTP 402).

Terms (Crucible Fund LLC, effective 2026-06-03): fees are billed up front for the full committed period and are non-refundable, including unused reservations and early termination; promotional credits may be modified or withdrawn at any time.
VM layout 'split' (default, two 5 CPU / 8 GiB VMs) or 'whole' (one 10 CPU / 16 GiB VM) at the same per-Mac price; layout changes need zero active sandboxes.

fleet.raise: Self-serve reservations are capped by currently free Macs (API returns 409 reservation_capacity_unavailable); API-key (SDK) reservations are limited to 1 Mac each; bulk fleets or long-term capacity by email request from the dashboard.
fleet.verification: Signup provides $100 starter credit with no card.
fleet.notes: Reservations are physical Macs for at least 24 hours, each allowing 2 simultaneous sandbox VMs. No account-wide reservation limit verified. Do not confuse provider inventory or per-host two-VM licence limit with account quota; stock and credits constrain fleets.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When you `delete()` (or your sandbox times out), the gateway throws away the dirty VM and clones a fresh one in the background.
snapshot_auto.note: Idle-reaped (ephemeral=true, ~2 min idle) or timed-out sandboxes and all sandboxes at reservation end_at are destroyed, not saved. State survives only via an explicit snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: macOS snapshots are portable disk deltas. When you create one, the gateway pulls the snapshot artifact from the source Mac Mini; when you launch from it, the gateway pushes that artifact to whichever reserved Mini claims the new VM.
snapshot_on_demand.note: POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/snapshots on a running sandbox ('Preserves disk state'); disk only, no memory. New sandboxes boot from it via create(snapshot=version) on any reserved Mac (template/fork, homepage: 'Snapshot a sandbox. Fork it instantly.'). Must match reservation layout and base image.

harness_api.quote: The `agents` extra installs the agent runtime plus model-provider dependencies (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, LiteLLM).
harness_api.note: The prebuilt computer-use agents (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OSWorld/generic via LiteLLM) run client-side in your Python process and drive the VM through the mouse/keyboard/screenshot API; no API to start/stream/resume an agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) inside the VM. Trajectory replay API (POST /v1/me/tasks/{id}/replay) re-executes recorded human actions, not an agent.

ingress_rules.quote: `vnc_url` from create or snapshot restore contains a sandbox-scoped viewer token, not your account key. The link expires within one hour, or earlier at the reservation's `end_at`
ingress_rules.note: No public ports/preview URLs. Access only through the authenticated gateway: SSH via a WebSocket proxy to sshd (API-key auth; supports -L port forwarding), VNC via expiring sandbox-scoped tokens ('Anyone holding the link can view and control that sandbox until it expires'). No IP allowlists or custom port exposure. Note PyPI README still warns vnc_url contains the account key (older SDK text).

secret_proxy.quote: sign into accounts (email, GitHub, a web app)
secret_proxy.note: No secret store or credential-injection proxy. Docs recommend signing into accounts by hand over VNC and baking the logins into a disk snapshot, i.e. credentials live inside the VM.

volume_attach.quote: `disk_gib` must be the image's disk size: disks are not resized at create.
volume_attach.note: Full OpenAPI spec has no volume/mount endpoints; storage is the VM image disk on the Mac's 512 GB SSD; files move via upload/download APIs.

volume_shared.note: No shared filesystem/volume concept; snapshots (disk deltas) are the only way to share state between sandboxes.
